llm.summary: This VMware policy skill is coherent and disclosed, but its documented fail-open behavior and simple policy bypass deserve user review before production use.

dimensions.detail: Local audit storage and rules files under ~/.vmware are purpose-aligned, but checking OPENAI_API_KEY presence for agent detection is broader than necessary even though the artifact says key values are not stored.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill installs as a uv package named vmware-policy, is not user-invocable, and exposes a CLI/library rather than MCP tools in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The docs state that missing rules, missing PyYAML, or VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 allow operations while preserving audit logging, which is under-scoped for a policy-enforcement layer covering high-impact VMware actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The audit database is persistent local state with rotation, and the policy layer supports a one-variable bypass plus fail-open defaults without strong guardrails or prominent production warnings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is audit logging, policy checks, and sanitization for VMware skills, and the documented components align with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before using it in production. Configure ~/.vmware/rules.yaml immediately, ensure PyYAML is installed, restrict who can set VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED, protect ~/.vmware/audit.db and exported logs, and consider replacing OPENAI_API_KEY-based agent detection with an explicit non-secret marker.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: Agent detection is expected for audit attribution, and the artifact says only the detected agent name is stored, but using OPENAI_API_KEY presence is unnecessarily secrets-adjacent.
[SQP-2] unexpected: A single VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 environment variable bypasses all policy checks; this is disclosed and logged, but it weakens the core enforcement function without documented production-grade controls.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit export is part of the skill purpose, but the CLI examples do not warn that exported audit records can contain operational metadata and should be handled as sensitive.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide says no rules file means all operations are allowed, which is a fail-open default for a policy component and is not clearly framed as a security risk.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The troubleshooting guide also says missing PyYAML silently allows all operations, adding another fail-open path for policy enforcement.
